claims: A compact runtime swap certificate is sound when every emitted field matches the canonical integer CPMM formula.
Certified runtime output cannot overdeliver the output reserve.
Runtime floor output is bounded by the favorable ceiling output, and the ceiling output is at most one unit above runtime output.
A certified fee-in-pool runtime step has exact K accounting and nondecreasing K under fee_bps <= 10000.
Route-level rounding budgets are sound when the checker supplies the declared recurrence certificate.
The zero-fee example witnesses the bridge on pool (1000,1000) with gross input 100.
proof_method: reuse of FeeAwareBatchKGap single-step exact K-gap accounting

boundaries: This bridge proves soundness for the mathematical certificate shape, not that any specific Python/Rust/Solidity implementation emits this exact certificate.
Fixed-width machine arithmetic still needs a separate representation/no-overflow bridge to natural-number semantics.
Route rounding budget soundness is abstract over the route metric; the runtime must define and check gap in the same units.
The bridge does not cover authorization, oracle freshness, route discovery, settlement attestation validity, or cross-pool graph completeness.
